tips.title: Recovery between sessions
tips.body:
Muscles and joints like a gap after a session. On GLP1 Life that gap is a rest day in the programme, a walk around the house, or an early night. Soreness that eases as you move is common. Pain that is sharp, one-sided, or still there the next morning is a reason to stop that move and choose the easier option next time.

A rest day is still part of the plan. You do not have to fill it. If you want to move, use the five-minute reset or a slow march rather than repeating the hardest session.

Eat something with protein when you can, drink water through the day, and sleep before you add more minutes. Check with your GP before you change how you eat or train. This is general information, not a meal plan or a medical instruction.

tips.title: Sleep when appetite is quieter
tips.body:
A smaller appetite can make evening meals easy to skip, and a skipped meal can make sleep lighter. Aim for a regular bedtime and a small, protein-containing snack if you are waking hungry, such as yoghurt or a piece of cheese with fruit. Keep the bedroom dark and cool, and leave the phone outside the bed if you can.

Exercise earlier in the day if a late session leaves you wired. A short mobility session is a better evening choice than a long march.

If sleep has been poor for more than a couple of weeks, or you feel faint when you stand up, talk to your GP. Do not use exercise to push through exhaustion. Check with your GP before you change how you eat or train. This is general information, not a meal plan or a medical instruction.

tips.title: A low-energy day still counts
tips.body:
Some days the plan will feel like too much. That is information, not a failure. Open the session, use the easier option on every move, or swap to the five-minute reset. A finished short session keeps the week streak. An abandoned hard session does not make you fitter.

Tell the planner how the session felt. Too hard makes the next one gentler. Too easy makes the next one a little slower and stronger, still without bouncing.

Compare yourself with your own last week, not with anyone else in the app. Coach Ava is an AI-generated instructor. The timed sessions in this library are written plans, not a live person watching you. Check with your GP before you change how you eat or train. This is general information, not a meal plan or a medical instruction.

tips.title: A gentle calorie deficit
tips.body:
Weight change, if that is your goal, usually comes from a modest gap between the energy you eat and the energy you use. A gentle deficit is a slightly smaller plate, not a day of skipping meals. Very low calorie diets and crash weeks are a poor fit when you are already eating less, and they are not what these workouts assume.

Keep a protein food at meals you do eat, include vegetables or fruit, and keep a carbohydrate you tolerate, such as potatoes, rice, or bread. The workouts add a little movement. They are not a licence to eat very little.

The calorie figure on a workout is an estimate from a standard formula. It is not a target to "earn" food, and it is not measured from your body. If you are losing weight very quickly, feeling cold, dizzy, or unwell, stop and speak to your GP or a registered dietitian. Check with your GP before you change how you eat or train. This is general information, not a meal plan or a medical instruction.

tips.title: Protein when meals are smaller
tips.body:
Smaller meals can mean less protein unless you plan for it. A practical pattern is a protein food at each meal you eat: eggs, yoghurt, milk, fish, chicken, tofu, beans, or cheese. You do not need a powder. If you use one, treat it as a food, read the label, and ask your GP or dietitian if it suits you.

Spread protein across the day rather than saving it for one large meal you may not finish. If nausea makes solid food difficult, a yoghurt or a milky drink can be easier than a dry piece of meat.

This app does not set a gram target for you. Needs differ, and a prescriber or dietitian can set one if you need it. Check with your GP before you change how you eat or train. This is general information, not a meal plan or a medical instruction.

tips.title: Hydration through the day
tips.body:
Thirst can be easy to miss when you are eating less often. Keep a glass of water nearby and sip through the session and afterwards. The home screen water goal is a prompt, not a medical fluid target.

Add drinks you enjoy: water, squash, tea, or milk. If you are dizzy on standing, cramping, or you have been sick, do not try to fix that with a large amount of water in one go. Contact your GP or NHS 111.

Alcohol is dehydrating and it is easy to under-eat around it. You do not need a sports drink for these low-impact sessions. Check with your GP before you change how you eat or train. This is general information, not a meal plan or a medical instruction.
